name: Upgrade plan, drain & schedule diagnosis
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture, Installation & Configuration (25%). Drill EVERY node-level kubeadm corner harder than the exam: inspect component versions, read the kubelet config and static-pod manifests, mint a worker join token, perform the drain/uncordon maintenance dance, renew control-plane certificates, read an upgrade plan, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix. All graded exactly on persistent node/cluster state.

questions.title: Drain then uncordon a node
questions.teach:
For node maintenance you `drain` (cordon + evict pods), do the work, then `uncordon` to let the scheduler use the node again: `kubectl drain <node>`, then `kubectl uncordon <node>`.

**Gotcha:** plain `drain` errors on real nodes — you need `--ignore-daemonsets`, plus `--force` to evict a bare (unmanaged) pod and `--delete-emptydir-data` if a pod uses emptyDir.
questions.prompt:
A bare Pod `drain-me` is pinned to worker $W2. Drain $W2 (evicting the workload), then uncordon it when "maintenance" is done.

Target: $W2 ends `schedulable` (`.spec.unschedulable` unset) AND no running `drain-me` pod remains on $W2.
questions.hint: `kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`, confirm with `kubectl get pods -o wide`, then `kubectl uncordon "$W2"`.
questions.solution:
kubectl drain "$W2" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl uncordon "$W2"
kubectl get node "$W2"

verification.description: $W2 is schedulable and holds no running drain-me pod

questions.title: Read a kubeadm upgrade plan
questions.teach:
`kubeadm upgrade plan` is a READ-ONLY report: it lists which versions you can upgrade to and the components it would bump. You run it before `kubeadm upgrade apply v1.X.Y`. The plan reasons about the running server (apiserver) version, which `kubectl version` reports.

**Gotcha:** parse the version with `kubectl version -o json` — the old `--short` flag was removed.
questions.prompt:
On $CP, run `kubeadm upgrade plan` to read it. To prove the control plane is healthy and reporting a version, write the server (apiserver) version string to `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP.

Target: `/tmp/serverversion.txt` on $CP contains a `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` Kubernetes version.
questions.hint: `docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan`. Then capture the server version onto the node: `docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -oE "v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'`.
questions.solution:
docker exec "$CP" kubeadm upgrade plan
docker exec "$CP" sh -c 'kubectl --kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf version -o json | grep -oE "v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+" | head -1 > /tmp/serverversion.txt'
docker exec "$CP" cat /tmp/serverversion.txt

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Pod that won't schedule
questions.teach:
A Pod stuck `Pending` with no node is a scheduling problem. `kubectl describe pod

` Events show the reason — a common one is every candidate node being `unschedulable` (cordoned), so the scheduler has nowhere to place it. **Gotcha:** fix the NODE (uncordon it), not the pod — an already-created Pending pod schedules on its own once a matching node becomes schedulable.
questions.prompt:
Pod `maint-app` in `default` is stuck `Pending` — it is pinned (via nodeSelector) to a worker that is currently cordoned. Diagnose WHY it won't schedule and fix it so it runs. Do NOT delete or recreate the pod, and do NOT edit the pod's nodeSelector.

Target: pod `maint-app` is `Running` AND the worker it targets is schedulable.
questions.hint: `kubectl describe pod maint-app` and `kubectl get nodes` — one worker shows `SchedulingDisabled`. That's $W1. Uncordon it: `kubectl uncordon "$W1"`, then watch `kubectl get pod maint-app -o wide`.
questions.solution:
kubectl describe pod maint-app
kubectl get nodes
# $W1 is cordoned (SchedulingDisabled) and maint-app's nodeSelector pins it there
kubectl uncordon "$W1"
kubectl get pod maint-app -o wide

verification.description: maint-app is Running and its target worker ($W1) is schedulable
